title: Conjectures on the roots and interlacing of Lambert W-function polynomials
statement:
Let $L_n(X)$ and $L_{n,k}(X)$ be the polynomial families defined earlier in the paper, and let the roots of a polynomial be ordered decreasingly when indexed by $j$. For $k\leq 0$, interpret $L_{n,k}(X)$ as $L_n^{(1-k)}(X)$. **Root and interlacing conjectures.** The roots of $L_n(X)$ are all nonnegative real and are at most $n+\log(n)+\gamma+O(1/n)$; more generally, its $j$th root is asymptotic to

$$
\frac{n}{j}+\sum_{j\leq m\leq n}\frac{1}{m}.
$$

The roots of $L_n(X)$ and $L_{n+1}(X)$ interlace. More generally, for $k\geq 1$, the roots of $L_{n,k}(X)$ are all nonnegative real, and their maximum has an asymptotic expansion

$$
n+\log(n)+\gamma+k-1+\frac{C_0(k)}{n}+\frac{C_1(k)}{n^2}+\cdots,
$$

where $C_m(k)$ is a polynomial of degree $m$ in $k$, and $C_0(k)$ is independent of $k$; the same assertion holds for $k\leq 0$ under the interpretation above. These conjectures concern the zero distribution and asymptotic behavior of the polynomial families arising in the branch expansions of the Lambert $W$ function. The paper presents them as additional properties requiring proof; the notation and precise prior definitions of $L_n(X)$ and $L_{n,k}(X)$ should be checked against the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.11698

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).
source_name: Henri Cohen, “Lambert W-Function Branch Identities”, arXiv:2012.11698 (2021).
